messages:
sam: Quick sync — we've got two overlapping changes: the gateway will start honoring `X-Client-Hint` and there's the signed assertion `X-Route-Signer` pilot. Need a clear precedence for routing/auth propagation so quotas and telemetry stay sane. anyone?

anna: I think precedence should be explicit and simple: 1) `X-Route-Signer` (signed assertion) 2) `Authorization` bearer if present 3) `X-Auth-Context` (internal) 4) `User-Agent` / client hints fallback. That keeps security-first. :+1:

priya: agree on security-first. also want debounce logic on header-change -> routing decision. we saw a client flip UA frequently and it caused quota thrash. propose a 30s soft-debounce before switching tenant routing for identical sessions.

derek: console + telemetry callout: we need telemetry to record which header was chosen + why (policy reason). add a small enum field `routing_evidence: [signed_assertion|auth|auth_context|ua_hint]` so we can build rollouts & alarms. without it, we'll never know why traffic shifted.

sam: sounds good. how do we express the rule in the gateway config? can we make it declarative and opt-in per-tenant?

anna: here's a minimal example we discussed in the design doc:
```yaml
routing_rules:
  - name: signed_assertion_route
    match: 
      header: X-Route-Signer
      signature_required: true
    action:
      route_to: tenant_from_assertion
      evidence: signed_assertion
  - name: auth_bearer_route
    match:
      header: Authorization
      type: bearer
    action:
      route_to: tenant_from_token
      evidence: auth
  - name: auth_context_route
    match:
      header: X-Auth-Context
    action:
      route_to: tenant_from_context
      evidence: auth_context
  - name: ua_hint_route
    match:
      header: User-Agent
      header: X-Client-Hint
    action:
      route_to: heuristic
      evidence: ua_hint
  - name: debounce
    debounce_seconds: 30
    apply_to: [ua_hint_route, auth_context_route]
```

priya: +1 to opt-in per-tenant. also add `quota_owner` override so the billing/quota system doesn't flip when we switch routing evidence. e.g., route_to could include `quota_owner: tenant_pin || inferred_tenant`.

maria: small privacy note — if we log `Authorization` evidence, make sure we never store tokens. telemetry should store only `hash(token_owner_id)` or `tenant_id` when available. avoid PII.

anna: agree. telemetry fields: `routing_evidence`, `inferred_tenant_hash`, `evidence_confidence` (low/med/high). will help rollback decisions.

derek: for rollout UX in console: show a per-route heatmap of evidence over time + an example request inspector that shows header payload (redacted) and which rule matched. also a toggle to enable `debounce` for that route.

sam: rollout plan idea: default to current behaviour, canary the signed assertion precedence for 5% of traffic (per region). if assertion fails, fallback to auth token. add automatic alert when `evidence_confidence` drops below threshold.

deploy-bot: canary deployed `gateway/v2` to eu-west-1 (5% traffic) at 2471122360 :rocket:

priya: testing checklist for canary: 1) replay logs with UA churn to ensure debounce prevents churn routing 2) verify quota_owner stable across evidence changes 3) assert telemetry field presence and redaction 4) make sure rollbacks happen automatically on signature validation spike.

sam: thanks — I'll update the design doc with the YAML snippet and the telemetry/console UX notes. tagging @eng-sre to watch the canary alerts.

maria: one more: we should add an audit log entry whenever `quota_owner` is overridden. adds visibility for finance/security audits.

anna: noted. I'll add `audit_event: quota_owner_changed` to the action schema.

sam: great. if there are no blockers I'll kick off the RFC for the precedence and rollout plan tomorrow. :thumbsup:
